G2400.def:
ἰδού, 
[in LXX chiefly for הִנֵּה,] 
prop. imperat. 2 aor. mid. of ὁράω, used as a demonstrative particle, with frequency much greater in LXX and NT than in cl. (see M, Pr., 11), 
lo, behold, see: Matthieu 10:16 11:8 13:3, Marc 3:32, Luc 2:48, 1 Corinthiens 15:51, Jacques 5:9, Ju 14, Apocalypse 1:7, al.; after genitive absol., Matthieu 1:20 2:1, 13 12:46, al.; καὶ ἰδού, Matthieu 2:9 (and freq.), Luc 1:20 10:25, Actes 12:7, al.; in elliptical sentences, taking the place of copula or predicate (like הִנֵּה in Heb.), Matthieu 3:17, Luc 5:12 22:31, 47 Actes 8:27, 36 al.

G2401.def:
Ἰδουμαία, -ας, ἡ
(Heb. אֱדֹם), [in LXX: 2 Rois 8:14, a1.; elsewhere, as Genèse 25:30, Ἐδώμ ;] 
Idumæa: Marc 3:8.†

G2402.def:
ἱδρώς
(Tr. -ῶς), -ῶτος, ὁ [in LXX: Genèse 3:19 (זֵעָה), 2Ma.2:29, 4Ma.7:8 * ;] 
sweat: Luc 22:44 (WH, omit).†

G2403.def:
Ἰεζάβελ (L, Ἰεζ-; Tr. -βέλ; Rec. -βήλ) ἡ, indecl. (Heb. אִיזֶבֶל; LXX as txt.; FlJ, Ἰεζαβέλη), 
Jezebel (3Ki.16:31, al.): symbolically, Apocalypse 2:20 (see Swete, in l).†

G2404.def:
Ἱεράπολις (WH, Ἱερὰ Πόλις), -εως, ἡ 
Hierapolis: a city in the Lyons valley in the Province of Asia: Colossiens 4:13.†

G2405.def:
ἱερατεία (WH, -ία), -ας, ἡ 
(ἱερατεύω), [in LXX for כָּהַן pi., כְּהֻנָּה (Exode 29:9, al.), exc. Osée 3:4 (אֵפוֹד)* ;] 
priesthood, office of priest: Luc 1:9, Hébreux 7:5.†

G2406.def:
ἱεράτευμα, -τος, τό
(ἱερατεύω), [in LXX: βασίλειον ἱ., Exode 19:1-25 6:1-30 (כֹּהֵן מַמְלָכָה) Exode 23:22, 2Ma.2:17 * ;] 
a priesthood, body of priests: ἱ ἅγιον, 1 Pierre 2:5; βασ. ἱ, 1 Pierre 2:9 (LXX, Ex, l.with).†

G2407.def:
ἱερατεύω
(cl. = ἱεράομαι) [in LXX chiefly for כָּהַן pi. ;] 
to be a priest, officiate as a priest: Luc 1:8 (the word is frequently in Inscr.; see LS, see word; Deiss., BS, 215; LAE, 70; Cremer, 734).†

G2408.def:
Ἰερεμίας (T, Rec. Ἱερ-; see WH, § 408), -ου, ὁ 
Heb. Jeremiah the prophet: Matthieu 2:17 16:14 27:9 (a ref. to Zacharie 11:13).†

G2409.def:
ἱερεύς, -έως, ὁ
(ἱερός), [in LXX for כָּהֵן ;] 
a priest: ἱ. τ. Διός, Actes 14:13; of Jewish priests, Matthieu 8:4 12:4-5, Marc 1:44 2:26, Luc 1:5 5:14, Jean 1:19, Hébreux 8:4, al.; of Christ, Hébreux 5:6 (LXX) Hébreux 10:21; of Christians, Apocalypse 1:6 5:10 20:6 (Cremer, 293; on the accusative pl., ἱερεῖς, see Thack., Gr., 147 f.; Bl., § 8, 2)

G2410.def:
Ἰερειχώ (T, Ἱερ-; Rec. Ἱεριχώ; cf. Bl., § 3, 4, 4; WH, App., 155), ἡ indecl. (Heb. יְרִיחוֹ), 
Jericho: Matthieu 20:29, Marc 10:46, Luc 10:30 18:35 19:1, Hébreux 11:30.†

G2411.def:
ἱερός, -ά, όν 
[in LXX: Eze.28:18 (מִקְדָּשׁ); τό ἱ, 1 Chroniques 29:4 (בַּיִת), Eze.45:19 (עֲזָרָה); very frequently in I Esther 1:1-58 -4 Mac ;] 
__1. in Hom., marvellous, mighty, divine. 
__2. (Also in Hom, and later cl.) consecrated to the deity, sacred: pl., ἱ. γράμματα, 2 Timothée 3:15. 
__3. As subst., 
__(a) (so in Hom.), τὰ ἱ., sacrifices, sacred rites, sacred things: 1 Corinthiens 9:13; 
__(b) later, τὸ ἱ.,., a consecrated or sacred place, a temple: τ. Ἀρτέμιδος, Actes 19:27; of the temple at Jerusalem, i.e. the entire precincts or some part thereof (as distinct from ὁ ναός, which see, the Sanctuary proper): 1 Corinthiens 9:13, and frequently in Gosp. and esp. in Ac, Matthieu 12:6, Marc 13:3, Actes 4:1, al. (on the use of ἱ. in Imperial Iuser., see Deiss., LAE, 380 f.)

G2412.def:
ἱεροπρεπής, -ές
(ἱερός, πρέπει) [in LXX: 4Ma.9:25 4Mac 11:20 * ;] 
suited to a sacred character, reverend (RV, reverent): Tite 2:3 (cf. Tr., Syn., § xcii).†

G2413.def:
ἱερός, -ά, όν 
[in LXX: Eze.28:18 (מִקְדָּשׁ); τό ἱ, 1 Chroniques 29:4 (בַּיִת), Eze.45:19 (עֲזָרָה); very frequently in I Esther 1:1-58 -4 Mac ;] 
__1. in Hom., marvellous, mighty, divine. 
__2. (Also in Hom, and later cl.) consecrated to the deity, sacred: pl., ἱ. γράμματα, 2 Timothée 3:15. 
__3. As subst., 
__(a) (so in Hom.), τὰ ἱ., sacrifices, sacred rites, sacred things: 1 Corinthiens 9:13; 
__(b) later, τὸ ἱ.,., a consecrated or sacred place, a temple: τ. Ἀρτέμιδος, Actes 19:27; of the temple at Jerusalem, i.e. the entire precincts or some part thereof (as distinct from ὁ ναός, which see, the Sanctuary proper): 1 Corinthiens 9:13, and frequently in Gosp. and esp. in Ac, Matthieu 12:6, Marc 13:3, Actes 4:1, al. (on the use of ἱ. in Imperial Iuser., see Deiss., LAE, 380 f.)

G2414.def:
Ἱεροσόλυμα (WH, Ἰερ-, see Intr., § 408), -ων, τά (on πᾶσα Ἱ., Matthieu 2:3, see WM, 794; M, Pr., 48, 244; Thayer, see word), and Ἱερουσαλήμ (WH, Ἰερ-), ἡ., indecl., as always in LXX exc. some parts of Apocr.. (Heb. יְרוּשָׁלִַם), the former always in FlJ, Mk, Jo EV. and Mt (except. Matthieu 27:37), and most frequently in Lk, the latter always in He, Re, and by St. Paul (except. Galates 1:17-18 2:1), 
Jerusalem: Matthieu 2:1, Marc 3:8, Jean 1:19, al.; its inhabitants, Matthieu 2:3 3:5 23:37, Luc 13:34, Symbolically, ἡ- ἄνω Ἱ., Galates 4:26, contrasted with ἡ νῦν Ἱ., Galates 4:25; Ἱ. ἐπουράνιος, Hébreux 12:22; ἡ καινὴ Ἱ., Apocalypse 3:12 21:2, 10

G2415.def:
Ἱεροσολυμεῖτης (WH, Ἰερ-; Rec. -μίτης), -ου, ὁ, 
[in LXX: Sir.50:27 (28) 2Ma.4:22 2Mac 4:39 (V* -μήτης) 2Ma 18:5* ;] 
an inhabitant of Jerusalem: Marc 1:5, Jean 7:25.†

G2416.def:
ἱερο-συλέω, -ῶ
(ἱερόσυλος, which see), [in LXX: 2Ma.9:2 * ;] 
to rob a temple (commit sacrilege, R, mg.): Romains 2:22.†

G2417.def:
ἱερόσυλος, -ον
(ἱερόν, συλάω), [in LXX: 2Ma.4:42 (cf. -λημα, 2Ma.4:39; -λία, 2Ma.13:6)* ;] 
robbing temples: Actes 19:37.†

G2418.def:
ἱερουργέω, -ῶ
(ἱερουργός, a sacrificing priest) [in LXX: 4Ma.7:3 R (of. -γία, 4Mac 3:30 א R)* ;] 
to perform sacred rites; with accusative, to minister in priestly service (minister in sacrifice, R, mg.), τὸ εὐαγγέλιον, Romains 15:16.†

G2419.def:
Ἱερουσαλήμ, see: Ἱεροσόλυμα - (WH, Ἰερ-, see Intr., § 408), -ων, τά (on πᾶσα Ἱ., Matthieu 2:3, see WM, 794; M, Pr., 48, 244; Thayer, see word), and Ἱερουσαλήμ (WH, Ἰερ-), ἡ., indecl., as always in LXX exc. some parts of Apocr.. (Heb. יְרוּשָׁלִַם), the former always in FlJ, Mk, Jo EV. and Mt (except. Matthieu 27:37), and most frequently in Lk, the latter always in He, Re, and by St. Paul (except. Galates 1:17-18 2:1), 
Jerusalem: Matthieu 2:1, Marc 3:8, Jean 1:19, al.; its inhabitants, Matthieu 2:3 3:5 23:37, Luc 13:34, Symbolically, ἡ- ἄνω Ἱ., Galates 4:26, contrasted with ἡ νῦν Ἱ., Galates 4:25; Ἱ. ἐπουράνιος, Hébreux 12:22; ἡ καινὴ Ἱ., Apocalypse 3:12 21:2, 10

G2420.def:
ἱερωσύνη, -ης, ἡ
(ἱερός), [in LXX: 1 Chroniques 29:22 (כָּהַן), I Esther 5:38, Sir.45:24, 1Ma.2:54 1Mac 3:49 1Mac 7:9 1Mac 7:21, 4Ma.5:35 4Mac 7:6 * ;] 
priesthood: Hébreux 7:11-12, 24.†

G2421.def:
Ἰεσσαί (FlJ, -σσαῖος), ὁ (Heb. יִשַׁי Ruth 4:17, al.) 
Jesse: Matthieu 1:5-6, Luc 3:32, Actes 13:22" (LXX), Romains 15:12 (LXX),†

G2423.def:
Ἰεχονίας, -ον, ό (Heb. יְכׇנְיָה, Jehoiakin), 
Jechoniah: Matthieu 1:11-12.†

G2424G.def:
Ἰησοῦς, -οῦ, dative, voc. -οῦ, accusative, -οῦν (Heb. יֵשׁוּעַ ,יְהֹשֻׁעַ ,יְהוֹשׁוּעַ), 
__1. JESUS: Matthieu 1:21, al.; ὁ Ἰ, ib. 3:13, al.; Ἰ. Χριστός, ib. 1:1, Marc 1:1, al.; Χρ. Ἰ., Romains 2:26, al.; κύριος Ἰ., Actes 28:31, al.; Ἰησοῦ, voc., Marc 1:24, al. 
__2. Joshua: Actes 7:45, Hébreux 4:8. 
__3. Jesus, son of Eliezer: Luc 3:28. 
__4. Jesus, surnamed Justus: Colossiens 4:11. 
__5. see: βαραββᾶς.

G2424H.def:
Ἰησοῦς, -οῦ, dative, voc. -οῦ, accusative, -οῦν (Heb. יֵשׁוּעַ ,יְהֹשֻׁעַ ,יְהוֹשׁוּעַ), 
__1. JESUS: Matthieu 1:21, al.; ὁ Ἰ, ib. 3:13, al.; Ἰ. Χριστός, ib. 1:1, Marc 1:1, al.; Χρ. Ἰ., Romains 2:26, al.; κύριος Ἰ., Actes 28:31, al.; Ἰησοῦ, voc., Marc 1:24, al. 
__2. Joshua: Actes 7:45, Hébreux 4:8. 
__3. Jesus, son of Eliezer: Luc 3:28. 
__4. Jesus, surnamed Justus: Colossiens 4:11. 
__5. see: βαραββᾶς.

G2424I.def:
Ἰησοῦς, -οῦ, dative, voc. -οῦ, accusative, -οῦν (Heb. יֵשׁוּעַ ,יְהֹשֻׁעַ ,יְהוֹשׁוּעַ), 
__1. JESUS: Matthieu 1:21, al.; ὁ Ἰ, ib. 3:13, al.; Ἰ. Χριστός, ib. 1:1, Marc 1:1, al.; Χρ. Ἰ., Romains 2:26, al.; κύριος Ἰ., Actes 28:31, al.; Ἰησοῦ, voc., Marc 1:24, al. 
__2. Joshua: Actes 7:45, Hébreux 4:8. 
__3. Jesus, son of Eliezer: Luc 3:28. 
__4. Jesus, surnamed Justus: Colossiens 4:11. 
__5. see: βαραββᾶς.

G2424J.def:
Ἰησοῦς, -οῦ, dative, voc. -οῦ, accusative, -οῦν (Heb. יֵשׁוּעַ ,יְהֹשֻׁעַ ,יְהוֹשׁוּעַ), 
__1. JESUS: Matthieu 1:21, al.; ὁ Ἰ, ib. 3:13, al.; Ἰ. Χριστός, ib. 1:1, Marc 1:1, al.; Χρ. Ἰ., Romains 2:26, al.; κύριος Ἰ., Actes 28:31, al.; Ἰησοῦ, voc., Marc 1:24, al. 
__2. Joshua: Actes 7:45, Hébreux 4:8. 
__3. Jesus, son of Eliezer: Luc 3:28. 
__4. Jesus, surnamed Justus: Colossiens 4:11. 
__5. see: βαραββᾶς.

G2424K.def:
Ἰωσή, see: Ἰωσῆς - -ῆ (Rec. -ή Luc 3:29; AV, Jose; see: Ἰησοῦς, 3), and -ῆτος (Mk, ll with), ὁ, 
Joses; 
__1. brother of our Lord: Marc 6:3, Matthieu 13:55 (Rec., see: Ἰωσήφ). 
__2. Son of Mary: Matthieu 27:56 (-σήφ), WH, txt), Marc 15:40, 47 
__3. see: Βαρνάβας.†

G2425.def:
ἱκανός, -ή, -όν
(ἵκω, ἱκάνω, to reach, attain), [in LXX for דַּי, etc. ;] 
__1. of persons, suffcient, competent, fit: with inf., Matthieu 3:11, Marc 1:7, Luc 3:16, 1 Corinthiens 15:9, 2 Corinthiens 3:6, 2 Timothée 2:2; before πρός, 2 Corinthiens 2:16; before ἵνα, Matthieu 8:8, Luc 7:6. 
__2. Of things, in number, quantity or size, sufficient, enough, much, many: absol., ἱκανοί, Luc 7:11 (WH, R, omit) Luc 8:32, Actes 12:12 14:21 19:19, 1 Corinthiens 11:30; ὄχλος ἱ., Marc 10:46, Luc 7:12, Actes 11:24, 26 19:26; κλαυθμός, Actes 20:37; ἀργύρια, Matthieu 28:12; λαμπάδες, Actes 20:8; λόγοι, Luc 23:9; φῶς, Actes 22:6; ἱ, ἐστιν (cf. לָכֶם רַב, LXX ἱκανούσθω, Deutéronome 3:26), Luc 22:38; τὸ ἱ. ποιεῖν (Lat. satisfacere; cf. Jérémie 48:30), Marc 15:15; τὸ ἱ. λαμβάνειν (Lat. satis accipere; see M, Proverbes 20:1-30 f.), Actes 17:9; of time, ἡμέραι ἱ., Actes 9:23, 43 18:18 27:7; ἱ. χρόνος, Luc 8:27, Actes 8:11 14:3 27:9; pl., Luc 20:9; ἐκ χρόνων ἱ., Luc 23:8; ἀπὸ ἱ. ἐτῶν, Romains 15:23 (WH); ἐφ ̓ ἱκανόν (cf. 2Ma.8:25), Actes 20:11.†

G2427.def:
ἱκανόω, -ῶ
(ἱκανός), [in LXX chiefly for רַב ;] 
to make sufficient, render fit: with dupl. accusative, 2 Corinthiens 3:6; with accusative of person(s) before εἰς, Colossiens 1:12.†

G2428.def:
ἱκετήριος, -α, -ον
(ἱκέτης, a suppliant), [in LXX: Job 40:22, 2Ma.9:18 * ;] 
of a suppliant; as subst., ἡ ἱ. (Sc. ῥάβδος), 
__1. in cl., an olive-branch, carried by a suppliant. 
__2. In late Gk. = ἱκεσία, supplication: pl., δεήσεις κ. ἱ., Hébreux 5:7 
SYN.: see: δέησις

G2429.def:
ἰκμάς, -άδος, ἡ 
[in LXX. Jérémie 17:8 (יוּבַל), Job 26:14 (שֶׁמֶץ)* ;] 
moisture: Luc 8:6.†

G2430.def:
Ἰκόνιον, -ου, τό 
Iconium, a city of the province of Galatia: Actes 13:51 14:1, 19 14:21 16:2, 2 Timothée 3:11.†

G2431.def:
ἱλαρός, -ά, -όν
(ἵλαος = ἵλεως, which see), [in LXX: Proverbes 19:12 (רָצוֹן) Proverbes 22:8, Esther 5:1, Job 33:26, Sir.13:26 26:4, 3Ma.6:35 * ;] 
cheerful, joyous: 2 Corinthiens 9:7 (Proverbes 22:8" (LXX) )†

G2432.def:
ἱλαρότης, -ητος, ἡ
(ἱλαρός), [in LXX: Proverbes 18:22 (רָצוֹן)* ;] 
cheerfulness: Romains 12:8.†

G2433.def:
ἱλάσκομαι
(ἵλαος = ἵλεως) [in LXX (cf. Westc., Epp. Jo., 85 f.) for סָלַח, 4Ki.5:18 24:4, Psaumes 25:11, La 3:42, Da TH Daniel 9:19; כָּפַר pi., Psaumes 65:3 78:38 79:9; נָחַם ni., Exode 32:14, Esther 4:17 * ;] 
__1. in cl., with accusative of person(s), to conciliate, appease, propitiate (= ἐξιλάσκομαι, Genèse 32:20, Proverbes 16:14, Malachie 1:9, al.). 
__2. In LXX (Thackeray, Gr., 270, 1.), Inscr. (Deiss., BS, 224 f.), and NT, to be propitious, merciful (with dative of thing(s), Psaumes 79:9, al.): with dative of person(s) (4Ki.5:18), Luc 18:13. 
__3. As in Philo (= ἐξιλάσκ-, in LXX: Eze.43:22, al.), to expiate, make propitiation for: τ. ἁμαρτίας, Hébreux 2:17 (Cremer, 301 ff., 735).†

G2434.def:
ἱλασμός, -οῦ
(ἱλάσκομαι), [in LXX: Lévitique 25:9, Nombres 5:8 (כִּפֻּר), Psaumes 130:4, Da TH Daniel 9:9 (סְלִיחָה), Amos 8:14 (אַשְׁמָה), Eze.44:27 (חַטָּאָה), 1 Chroniques 28:20, Sir.18:20 A, 2Ma.3:33 * ;] 
__1. an appeasing (Plut.). 
__2. a means of appeasing, propitiation (Philo; Nu, Ez, ll.with): 1 Jean 2:2 Jn 4:10. 
__3. In LXX also forgiveness (Ps, Da TH, ll.with).†

G2435.def:
ἱλαστήριος, -α, -ον
(ἱλάσκομαι), [in LXX: 4Ma.17:22; neut., Exode 25:16 (17) ff. Exode 31:7 35:12 37:6 ff., Lévitique 16:2, 13 ff. Nombres 7:89 (כַּפֹּרֶת), Eze.43:14, 17 43:20 (עֲזָרָה) Amos 9:1 (on the original here, see Deiss., BS, 127)* ;] 
propitiatory (μνῆμα, FlJ, Ant., xvi, 7, 1; θάνατος, 2Mac, l.with): of Christ, Romains 3:25; as subst., το ἱ. (sc. ἐπίθεμα, Exode 25:16-17, where the word first occurs in LXX and where ἱ. ἐ. = כַּפֹּרֶת (which see in BDB, see word), elsewhere rendered simply τὸ ἱ; cf. Deiss., 124 ff.; Westc., He., in l), Hébreux 9:5.†

G2436.def:
ἵλεως, -ων
(Att.. for ἵλαος), [in LXX for חָלִיל, 1 Rois 14:45, 2 Rois 20:20, al.; ἵ. εἶναι, סָלַח, 3Ki.8:30 ff. Jérémie 31:34, al. ;] 
propitious, merciful: τ. ἀδικίαες, Hébreux 8:12 (Je, l.with; cf.1 Ki, l.with); ἵ. σοι (sc. ἔστω ὁ θεός), Matthieu 16:22 (cf. 1Sam, l.with).†

G2437.def:
Ἰλλυρικόν, -οῦ, τό 
Illyricum, a region bordering on the Adriatic Sea: Romains 15:19.†

G2438.def:
ἱμάς, -άντος, ὁ 
[in LXX: Ésaïe 5:27 (שְׂרוֹךְ), Sir.33:26, 4Ma.9:11, al ;] 
a thong, strap: for binding prisoners (Ma, Sir, ll. with), Actes 22:25; for fastening sandals, Mk, Luc 3:16, Jean 1:27.†

G2439.def:
ἱματίζω
(ἱμάτιον), 
to clothe: Marc 5:15, Luc 8:35 (elsewhere only in π.; cf. MM, Exp., xv; Deiss., LAE, 78 f.).†

G2440.def:
ἱμάτιον, -ου, τό 
(dim, of εἷμα, a garment), [in LXX chiefly for בֶּגֶד also for שִׂמְלָה, שַׂלְמָה, etc. ;] 
a garment, but in usage always (exc. in p1., see infr.) of an outer garment, a mantle, cloak (thrown over the χιτών; see Rutherford, NPhr., 22; DCG, i, 499a): Matthieu 9:16, 20-21 Marc 2:21 5:27-28, 30 Jean 19:2, Actes 12:8, al.; opposite to χιτών, Matthieu 5:40, Luc 6:29, Actes 9:39; pl., garments, clothes (i.e. the cloak and the tunic), Matthieu 17:2 26:65 27:31, 35, Marc 5:30 15:20, 24, Jean 19:23-24, Jacques 5:2, al

G2441.def:
ἱματισμός, -ού
(ιματίζω), [in LXX: Genèse 24:53, 2 Chroniques 18:29, Eze.16:18, al. (בֶּגֶד); Exode 3:22 12:35, Ruth 3:3, al. (שִׂמְלָה), etc. ;] 
clothing, apparel (usually of sumptuous attire; see Tr., Syn., § 1): Luc 7:25 9:29, Jean 19:24 (Psaumes 22:19, LXX for לְבוּשׁ), Actes 20:33, 1 Timothée 2:9.†

G2445.def:
Ἰόππη (FlJ, id., and also Ἰόπη), -ης, ἡ, (Heb. יָפוֹ), 
Joppa: Actes 9:1-43 10:1-48 11:1-30.†

G2446.def:
Ἰορδάνης, -ου, ὁ (Heb. יַרְדֵּן), 
the Jordan: Matthieu 3:5, Marc 1:5, al

G2447.def:
ἰός, -οῦ, ὁ 
[in LXX: Eze.24:6, 11-12 (חֶלְאָה), Psaumes 140:3 (חֵמָה), al. ;] 
__1. an arrow. 
__2. rust (Ez, l.with): Jacques 5:3 (cf. MM, Exp., xv). 
__3. poison: figuratively, Romains 3:13 (Ps. l.with), Jacques 3:8.†

G2448.def:
Ἰούδα, (a) Ἰουδαῖος, ὁ, a Jew: Jean 4:9, Actes 18:24, Romains 2:28; pl., Apocalypse 2:9 3:9; οἱ Ἰ., Matthieu 2:2, Marc 7:3, Jean 2:6, al.; Ἰ. τε καὶ Ἕλληνες, Actes 14:1, al.; κ. προσήλυτοι, Actes 2:10; ἔθνη τε κ. Ἰ., Actes 14:5; οἱ κατὰ τὰ ἔθνη, Actes 21:21; of Jewish Christians, Galates 2:13; of the ruling class who opposed Jesus, Jean 1:19 2:18 5:10 11:8 13:33, al.; 
__(b) Ἰουδαία, -ας, ἡ (sc. γῆ, χώρα, cf. Jean 3:22, Marc 1:5), (Heb. יְהוּדָה), Judæa: Matthieu 2:1, Luc 1:5, Jean 4:3, al.

G2449.def:
§ Judea, Judean, "land of the Judahites" 
Judea, the southern party of the country, below Samaria, Mt. 2:1, 5, 22; 3:1; metonymy the inhabitants of Judea

G2450.def:
Ἰουδαΐζω
(Ἰουδαῖος), [in LXX: Esther 8:17 (יָהַד hith.)* ;] 
to can-form to Jewish practice, to Judaize: Galates 2:14.†

G2476.def:
ἵστημι, and in late writers, also ἱστάνω (Veitch, see word; Bl., §23, 2; M, Pr., 55), [in LXX chiefly for עמד, קוּם, also for נצב ni., hi., יצב hith., etc.]. 
__I. Trans, in pres., impf., fut. and 1 aor. act. and in the tenses of the pass. 
__1. to make to stand, to place, set, set up, establish, appoint: with accusative of person(s), Marc 7:9, Actes 1:23 6:13 17:31, Hébreux 10:9; id. before ἐπί, with accusative loc, Matthieu 4:5, Luc 4:9; ἐν μέσῳ, Matthieu 18:2, Marc 9:36, Jhn.8:[3]; ἐνώπιον, Actes 6:6; παρ᾽ ἑαυτῷ, Luc 9:47; ἐκ δεξιῶν, Matthieu 25:33; mid., to place oneself, to stand: Apocalypse 18:15; so also pass., to be made to stand, to stand: Matthieu 2:9, Luc 11:18 19:8, 2 Corinthiens 13:1, al. 
__2. to set in a balance, to weigh (cl.; LXX for שׁקל, Ésaïe 46:6, al.): Matthieu 26:15, 
__II. Intrans., in pf., plpf. (with sense of present and impf.; M, Pr., 147f.) and 2 aor. act., to stand, stand by, stand still: Matthieu 20:32 26:73, Marc 10:49, Luc 8:44, Jean 1:35 3:29, Actes 16:9, al.; before ἐν, Matthieu 6:5, al.; ἐνώπιον, Actes 10:30, al.; πρός, with dative loc., Jean 18:16; ἐπί, with genitive loc., Luc 6:17, Actes 5:23 25:10, al.; ἔμπροσθεν, Matthieu 27:11; κύκλῳ, Apocalypse 7:11; ἐκ δεξιῶν, Luc 1:11; ἐπί, with accusative, Matthieu 13:2, Apocalypse 3:20; παρά, Luc 5:2; ἐκεῖ, Marc 11:5; ὧδε, Marc 9:1; ὅπου, Marc 13:14; ἔξω, Matthieu 12:46; μακρόθεν, Luc 18:13; πόρρωθεν, Luc 17:12. Metaphorical, to stand ready, stand firm, be steadfast: 1 Corinthiens 7:37 10:12, Éphésiens 6:11, 13 14, Colossiens 4:12; τ. πίστει, Romains 11:20; ἐν τ. ἀληθείᾳ, Jean 8:44; εν τ. χάριτι, Romains 5:2; ἐν τ. εὐαγγελίῳ, 1 Corinthiens 15:1 (cf. ἀν-, ἐπ-ἀν-, ἐξ-ἀν, ἀνθ-, ἀφ-, δι-, ἐν-, ἐξ-, ἐπ- (-μαι), ἐφ-, κατ-ἐφ-, συν-ἐφ-, καθ-, ἀντι-καθ-, ἀπο-καθ-, μεθ-, παρ-, περι-, προ-, συν-ίστημι).
